passage:
Vasudha: Ammi called. she wants me home every weekend now 😔
Pooja: every weekend? you have your project
Vasudha: I know. she says a good daughter visits. I felt awful and said okay
Pooja: do you want to go every weekend?
Vasudha: no. I want to go once a month and call her on Sundays
Pooja: tell her that. calmly. maybe explain the project and say you'll visit when it's done
Vasudha: she'll say I'm being cold
Pooja: maybe at first. give her time. offer a plan: first visit next month, a long call every Sunday
Vasudha: ok. I'll try tomorrow, when she's had her tea 🙂
Pooja: good luck. tell me how it goes

qa.q: When will Vasudha talk to her mother?
qa.a: Vasudha plans to try tomorrow, when she's had her tea.

qa.q: What was Vasudha feeling after the call with Ammi?
qa.a: Vasudha felt awful and guilty, having said okay when she wanted less frequent visits. She also worries her mother will call her cold, so she is torn between love and her own limits.

qa.q: What could Vasudha try to explain her limit?
qa.a: Explain the project calmly, offer a plan such as a visit next month and a long Sunday call, and give her mother time.

qa.q: How might Vasudha's mother see the request?
qa.a: Her mother may take it as disrespect or coldness at first, since a good daughter visiting is important to her, though a warm plan may help.

grounding: A young adult limits family expectations about visits with a calm, warm plan, though it can feel disrespectful in some families.

passage: Raghav's father had run the hardware shop in the small town for thirty years, and everyone assumed Raghav would take over. On Sunday evening, Hemant, Raghav's older cousin, sat with him on the roof and said, "Papa is telling everyone you'll start at the counter in June." Raghav's stomach tightened. He'd been accepted for a diploma in animation in the city. "I love the shop," he said. "I love Papa. But I want to try this first." Hemant frowned, then nodded slowly. "Tell him gently. Not in front of everyone. And maybe say you'll help during the festival season." Raghav decided to speak to his father the next morning, over tea.

qa.q: Where did Raghav sit with Hemant?
qa.a: Raghav sat with Hemant on the roof.

qa.q: What was Raghav feeling on the roof?
qa.a: Raghav felt torn, since he loves the shop and his father but wants to try the animation diploma first. His tight stomach shows he fears disappointing his father.

qa.q: What could Raghav do to make the conversation gentler?
qa.a: Speak to his father privately over tea, explain calmly and offer to help during the festival season.

qa.q: How might Raghav's father see the refusal?
qa.a: His father may feel hurt or disrespected at first, since he has run the shop for thirty years and told others the plan, but warmth and time may help.

grounding: A young adult sets a limit on family expectations about career, with calm warmth, though it may feel disrespectful in some families.
